parts.title: Passage Reading
teacherDirections: Read the complete controlled passage. Passage history is explicitly unverified, so confirm it has not already been completed before using it. Ask all ten teacher-created questions in the required ladder.

data.passage:
Hundreds of years ago, over 2,000 miles of roads were built that stretched along the Pacific shores of South America. To whom do we give the credit for this connection of roads? The Inca civilization, that’s who!

The people of the Inca civilization were especially skilled at other things too. They could craft a bridge, a tunnel, or even a whole city. They could work with cloth, stone, and all kinds of metals. These talents led to the evolution of a massive kingdom. The Inca had special traditions. They had skill with math computations. And, they had great drive which led to many successes during their rule.

The Inca people planted many crops. In addition, these wise people could cure themselves of sickness long before medical science existed. Conditions such as physical illnesses and problems with emotions were addressed by the Inca in their own special ways.

The Inca people did not write down their legends like ourselves. However, mothers and fathers still passed along their collection of tales and traditions. They retold them to their children.

There is no question that the Inca was a nation of people with many skills. We may find ourselves thinking about contributions of the Inca for a long time.
